chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn Amirah from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman whom her husband divorced three times before consummating the marriage, he said: She is not permissible to him until she marries another husband, so it does not contradict the earlier reports which indicated that she becomes fully divorced (bayyinah) with one divorce, because the meaning in this report is that if he contracted marriage with her three times, divorcing her each time before consummation, then in this state she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on triple divorce before consummation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this report from Imam al-Sadiq to resolve the apparent contradiction between the general rule of *bayyinah* (irrevocable divorce) after a single pre-consummation divorce and the specific case of triple divorce. The scholar clarifies that while one divorce typically suffices for *bayyinah*, a triple divorce in this context imposes the stricter condition of *nikah jiddah* (marriage to another man) before the first husband can remarry her, thereby harmonizing the narrations through contextual specificity.
